source: «La tenuta de Franceschi di Seghetto», la Voce del popolo, storia&ricerca, issue 134, 23 May 2020 — with the family's entry in the Blasonario Giuliano (Unione degli Istriani), «Franceschi (de) — Seghetto, Capodistria, Umago», which is the fuller and more careful of the two and corrects two of the newspaper's dates.
honours: The family's own origin story: Feramondo de Franceschi, who fought Odoacer, and after the deposition of Romulus Augustulus in 476 withdrew to Padua and then Venice. Legend — but the name Ferramondo was still being given to sons of this house in the twentieth century.
Emigrated to Candia with the Venetian colonies, receiving fiefs from the Doge, and became noble feudatories of Crete.
The first de Franceschi actually proved in the nobiliary registers of the Archive of the Duke of Candia: Luca di Nicolò. His father Nicolò was castellan of Castel Milopotamo in 1500.
In the Veneto-Turkish war they defended the Cretan ports of Colus, Lemiores and Sabbionera with the vassals of their county, at their own expense.
Marcantonio de Franceschi is Secretary of the Council of Ten — the same office, a generation after Andrea de' Franceschi held the Grand Chancellorship.
Marcantonio Querini, Duke of Candia, confirms the privileges of mero e misto impero. Comital title, confirmed again in 1688.

The brothers Carlo, Giovanni Battista, Costantino and Domenico, sons of the late Lodovico, give the Republic one hundred thousand ducats. The Senate raises the family unanimously from the Order of Secretaries to the Sovereign Patrician Order and inscribes it in the Libro d'Oro.
Marcantonio Franceschi, a native of Candia, is living in Istria.
Aggregated to the nobility of Parenzo. (The newspaper gives 1774; the armorial 1744.)
Aggregated to the Noble Council of Capodistria.
Confirmed noble by the Emperor Francis I of Austria.
Giovanni Battista de Franceschi is Podestà of Umago.
The title of nobles of Capodistria recognised in the Official List of the Italian nobility.
wreck: In 1669, when Candia fell to the Turks, part of Morosini's galleys took aboard the Venetian families who had asked to be brought home. On the way the fleet met a terrible storm; the ships were wrecked, and only a small number of the refugees were saved. The de Franceschi were among the survivors.
estate: Venice settles thirty families in the Umago district under captain Vincenzo Chiucchel — Cuchich — of Šibenik, paying him six ducats a month for life and promising thirty ducats a family for livestock. Seghetto and neighbouring Giubba are part of that grant.
Chiucchel sells the estate to the Valier of Venice.
Nicolò and Marc'Antonio de Franceschi, sons of Giorgio, buy Seghetto with everything the noblewoman Caterina Bernardo, widow of Pietro Valier, held in Istria.
Umago grants them citizenship, for themselves and their descendants.
Marc'Antonio de Franceschi (1671–1758), civil and military physician, begins the house around which the whole complex grows.
The chapel of S. Costanza is already standing; it appears in an inventory of that year.

Giorgio de Franceschi (1788–1865), son of Marc'Antonio and grandson of Alvise, commissions the great works: a grand internal staircase in the east wing, decoration by the painter Michele Urban, and on the façade two giant pilasters and a tympanum bearing the family arms — the neoclassical front still there.
The east wing is added, holding on its ground floor a library of over four thousand volumes and the family archive.
Library and archive both devastated. The room that held them was partitioned into smaller ones.
On the initiative of the City of Umag, the stanzia of Seghetto enters the conservation programme.
guests: The Venetian admiral who led the fleet to its last victories, in the expeditions of 1769 and 1784 against the Barbary corsairs.
The Triestine father of Istrian historiography — and, two generations later, the scholarly predecessor of Carlo and Camillo De Franceschi of the other Istrian branch.
offices: Member of the General Council of the Department of Istria.
A physician; volunteered in the Risorgimento campaigns with Garibaldi.
Mayors of Umago across a century. Giovanni Battista was a scholar and collector of unpublished manuscripts on the town's history.
President of the Filarmonica Umaghese and of the Society of Mutual Aid; councillor of the Congregation of Charity, the Rural Bank and the Cooperative Purchasing Society.
An engineer. Built a brick works at Spinel, ruined by the Great War; designed and directed the church and campanile at Materada.
Commissioners of Umago through the Italian administration and the war.
arms: Troncato di azzurro e d'oro al leone al naturale, rampante — per fess azure and or, a lion rampant proper. Crest: the same lion issuant. Three variants are recorded: the lion argent over all with an archaic gold-and-azure mantling; azure, a lion proper gazing at a gold eight-pointed star on a green base; and per fess azure and or, a lion counterchanged. The Piacenza noble branch of 1802, confirmed 1830, bore the lion proper over all.
trade: Great landowners: wine, oil, cereals, timber, and birds both live and slaughtered. Behind the house stood the coach-house, the produce stores, the colonists' dwellings and a nineteenth-century oil mill, whose presses and dozen stone oil jars — the pile — survived until the press was converted into a dwelling about twenty years ago. In their free time the colonists formed a wind band under the maestro Pietro Moro, and it was, the paper says, of decent success.
